title: "Tidy" examples
description:
A little proof of concept..

In the tidyverse, existing variables are quoted. Non-existing are unquoted. 
Existing variables are usually first , new ones after. 

That is something that always confused me in tidytext. Like what variable is going to come out of this
```r
unnest_tokens(dat, word, words, "words")
```
It seems just a bit too cryptic for new users.

 I know the package is too "mature for breaking changes", but I thought that updating examples would help new users get on board with tidytext more easily, while keeping older users code intact. 

If you think that's a good idea, I will update other  `unnest_tokens()` examples!

Thanks for the great package!

Feel free to close if you don't think it is relevant.

Edit: in an "ideal" world, the input and output arguments would be switched. and output would warn or error on unquoted entry, but I think updating examples is sufficient.

title: `tidy.STM` with content variable in stm
description:
I realized that when then document-level `content` covariate is set in `stm`, the beta-list contains also the interaction coefficients besides the topic-term probabilities and provides a beta-matrix for each covariate separately, in which case `tidy.STM` returns a tibble where some topics/terms are NAs, and multiple values for topic-term combinations (exactly the number of levels in the covariate) - reprex below. 

So I restricted it to only return the beta-values and added a column to the beta tibble which indicates the covariate.

``` r
library(stm)
#> stm v1.3.6 successfully loaded. See ?stm for help. 
#>  Papers, resources, and other materials at structuraltopicmodel.com
library(tidytext)
topic_model_content <- stm(poliblog5k.docs, poliblog5k.voc, K = 20,
            prevalence = ~ rating + s(day), content = ~ rating,
            max.em.its = 3, data = poliblog5k.meta, init.type = "Spectral",
            verbose = F)
td_beta_content <- tidy(topic_model_content)
td_beta_content
#> # A tibble: 271,097 × 3
#>    topic term      beta
#>    <int> <chr>    <dbl>
#>  1    NA <NA>  0.000133
#>  2    NA <NA>  0.000292
#>  3    NA <NA>  0.000269
#>  4    NA <NA>  0.000536
#>  5    NA <NA>  0.000376
#>  6    NA <NA>  0.000109
#>  7    NA <NA>  0.000294
#>  8    NA <NA>  0.000101
#>  9    NA <NA>  0.000130
#> 10    NA <NA>  0.000246
#> # … with 271,087 more rows
```

title: Added new framework for `get_sentiments`
description:
Hi

Been working with tidytext the past month or so. The one think I found which was restricting my analysis was the incorporation of a new dictionary. So, after playing with the code a bit I designed a framework that I think works easier and helps to incorporate the idea of easily adding a dictionary to the `get_sentiments()` function.

The new framework relies on  named `lists` rather than having to filter a `data.frame`. To give you an idea on how I include new dictionaries, please see the code at the bottom. I believe this way of handling the dictionaries to be a bit easier, intuitive and should scale better when conducting large analysis using multiple dictionaries.

```
create_sentiment_dict <- function(){

  sentiments <- list()
  
  sentiments <- c("afinn", "bing", "nrc", "loughran") %>% map(~.x %>% tidytext::get_sentiments())
  names(sentiments) <- c("afinn", "bing", "nrc", "loughran")
  
  sentiments[["harvard_four"]] <- SentimentAnalysis::DictionaryGI %>%
    Map(cbind, word = ., sentiment = names(.)) %>%
    reduce(rbind) %>% tbl_df
  
  sentiments[["henry"]] <- SentimentAnalysis::DictionaryHE %>%
    Map(cbind, word = ., sentiment = names(.)) %>%
    reduce(rbind) %>% tbl_df
  
  sentiments[["loughran_mcDonald"]] <- SentimentAnalysis::DictionaryLM %>%
    Map(cbind, word = ., sentiment = names(.)) %>%
    reduce(rbind) %>% tbl_df
  
  sentiments[["qdap_pol"]] <- qdapDictionaries::key.pol %>%
    rename(., word = x, score = y)
  
  return(sentiments)
  
  #save(sentiments, file = "data/sentiments.rda")
}

```

title: Added support for 17 foreign languages & for custom dictionaries
description:
Added support for 17 foreign languages + it's now possible to pass a custom hunspell dictionary. List of default supported languages is returned with ```r supported_languages() [1] "english" "bulgarian" "croatian" "danish" "dutch" [6] "french" "german" "greek" "icelandic" "italian" [11] "norwegian" "polish" "portuguese_european" "russian" "slovenian" [16] "spanish" "swedish" "turkish" "custom" ``` tokenization is handled by modified functions from the {tokenizers} package (see utils.R and tokenizers_foreign.R) Foreign languages can be parsed as usual (ngrams, html, etc). Added a Vignette about foreign languages. Examples : ```r library(tidytext) library(dplyr) supported_languages() fr <- tibble::tibble(txt = c("C'est dans l'arrière-cuisine. On s'en sert pour ranger.", "On aime l'arrière-saison. On part toujours en vacances à ce moment")) fr %>% unnest_tokens(word, txt, lang = "french") # A tibble: 25 x 1 word 1 c 2 est 3 dans 4 l 5 arrière 6 cuisine 7 on 8 s 9 en 10 sert # ... with 15 more rows fr %>% unnest_tokens(ngram, txt, token = "ngrams", n = 2, lang = "french") # A tibble: 24 x 1 ngram 1 c est 2 est dans 3 dans l 4 l arrière 5 arrière cuisine 6 cuisine on 7 on s 8 s en 9 en sert 10 sert pour # ... with 14 more rows data_frame(row = 1:2, text = c("

Du text ici", "C'est l'ancien site")) %>% unnest_tokens(word, text, format = "html", lang = "french") # A tibble: 8 x 2 row word 1 1 du 2 1 text 3 1 ici 4 2 c 5 2 est 6 2 l 7 2 ancien 8 2 site tibble::tibble(txt = c("Mir geht’s nicht gut.", "Darf ich mit Kreditkarte bezahlen? ")) %>% unnest_tokens(word, txt, lang = "german") # A tibble: 10 x 1 word 1 mir 2 geht 3 s 4 nicht 5 gut 6 darf 7 ich 8 mit 9 kreditkarte 10 bezahlen # turkish tibble::tibble(txt = c("İyiyim teşekkür ederim, siz nasılsınız", "Türkçe konuşur musunuz?")) %>% unnest_tokens(word, txt, lang = "turkish") # A tibble: 8 x 1 word 1 i̇yiyim 2 teşekkür 3 ederim 4 siz 5 nasılsınız 6 türkçe 7 konuşur 8 musunuz #russian tibble::tibble(txt = c("Говорите, пожалуйста, медленнее. Вы говорите по-английски?", "К сожалению, мне (нам) пора идти.")) %>% unnest_tokens(word, txt, lang = "russian") # A tibble: 13 x 1 word 1 говорите 2 пожалуйста 3 медленнее 4 вы 5 говорите 6 по 7 английски 8 к 9 сожалению 10 мне 11 нам 12 пора 13 идти ``` With a custom dictionary ```r df_latin <- tibble(text = "Alea Jacta Est.") download.file("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/titoBouzout/Dictionaries/master/la.aff", "la.aff") unnest_tokens(df_latin, word, text, lang = "custom", dict = "la.aff") # A tibble: 3 x 1 word 1 alea 2 jacta 3 est ```

title: Fix tests for corrected tokenize_skip_ngrams()
description:
This pull request fixes two failing tests caused by an imminent release of v0.2 of the tokenizers package. The version 0.1.4 of the tokenizers package currently on CRAN has an incorrect implementation of skip n-grams. (See [this issue](https://github.com/ropensci/tokenizers/issues/24) for details.) The master branch of tokenizers has a fix. As a result the indices used in the tests are now incorrect and I have updated them.

Note that `tokenize_skip_ngrams()` now returns *vastly* more tokens, which is how it is supposed to work, but which might come as a surprise.

title: Order labels in facet_wrap with drlib::reorder_within
description:
In the tidytext book, graph labels often need to be reordered by the count. In fact, this struggle has been documented in a few blog posts:

- https://trinkerrstuff.wordpress.com/2016/12/23/ordering-categories-within-ggplot2-facets/
- https://drsimonj.svbtle.com/ordering-categories-within-ggplot2-facets

Including ggplot [issue #1902](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/1902) and [pull request #1917](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/pull/1917).

Currently, Hadley [suggests](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/1902#issuecomment-275180398) David Robinson's [solution](https://github.com/dgrtwo/drlib/blob/master/R/reorder_within.R) found in his personal library. 

I thought it might be useful to include this function within the tidytext package, since it is a common operation within the tidytext book, and it might be easier to find this function if it was in this package.

title: Add test for `.data` pronoun back in
description:
I'm having trouble getting **both** this usage:

```r
d %>% unnest_tokens(.data$word, .data$txt)
```

**And** this usage to work:

```r
d %>% unnest_tokens("word", "txt")
```

I think the problem is that the `.data` pronoun isn't really great for new columns being created, but [someone is using it that way in a package](https://github.com/oriolarques/GSEAmining/blob/master/R/gm_clust.R) to avoid CRAN check notes.


Current problems with the version with string inputs, because of [these embraces](https://github.com/juliasilge/tidytext/blob/master/R/unnest_tokens.R#L175-L183) I used for handling new columns:

``` r
library(tidytext)
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
d <- tibble(
  txt = c(
    "Because I could not stop for Death -",
    "He kindly stopped for me -",
    "The Carriage held but just Ourselves –",
    "And Immortality.",
    "We slowly drove – He knew no haste",
    "And I had put away",
    "My labor and my leisure too,",
    "For His Civility –"),
  group = c("a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "a", "c", "c")
)

d %>% unnest_tokens(token, txt)
#> # A tibble: 41 x 2
#>    group token  
#>    <chr> <chr>  
#>  1 a     because
#>  2 a     i      
#>  3 a     could  
#>  4 a     not    
#>  5 a     stop   
#>  6 a     for    
#>  7 a     death
```

title: Add back in test for using `.data` pronoun
description:
I'm having trouble getting **both** this usage:

```r
d %>% unnest_tokens(.data$word, .data$txt)
```

**And** this usage to work:

```r
d %>% unnest_tokens("word", "txt")
```

I think the problem is that the `.data` pronoun isn't really great for new columns being created, but [someone is using it that way in a package](https://github.com/oriolarques/GSEAmining/blob/master/R/gm_clust.R) to avoid CRAN check notes.

title: Fix `abort()` call
description:
I see in revdep checks:

```
Running the tests in ‘tests/testthat.R’ failed.
Last 13 lines of output:
  Actual message: "`class` must be a character vector."
```

`abort()` is now stricter regarding the sort of objects passed as `class` argument and this uncovered a bug in tidytext. You can fix it with this patch.

We plan to release rlang 1.0.0 within 2 to 4 weeks.
